Generals Murder Cover-Up?

By: Graham Coetzer | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Private prosecutor Gerrie Nel has accussed the SAPS and SANDF of colluding to protect two high ranking SANDF members from criminal prosecution in a kidnapping and assault and possibly murder case.

Unique Selling Point:
After the alleged kidnapping and assault of two men, Sibusiso Phetla and Jerome Lebaka, in February this year, the victims have never been heard of again and suspicions are that they were murdered. It has since come to light that Phetla and Lebaka were mistaken for burglars outside a SANDF general's home, where they were allegedly assaulted by soldiers protecting the general. Another general has also been implicated. While the soldiers who were under the command of the generals have been arrested and are facing charges of assault and kidnapping, the general's have not - raising concerns that the generals are being protected.

Summary:
According to a witness,(a man who drove them) Phetla and Lebaka got lost on their way to Thaba Tshwane in Pretoria in February. They ended up in Magasyn Street, in the Dequar Military Residential area. Kgaugelo, the driver, stopped the car next to a house. Unbeknownst to him, it was the home of Major General Hlongwa, a high ranking official in the SANDF. Apparently they stopped to phone for directions to their destination. As the men were making the phone call, they heard a gunshot from Maj Gen Hlongwa's house - apparently the General had fired the shot to scare them off. Almost immediately their car was surrounded by armed military personnel, guards on duty at the General's house.

General Hlongwa ordered his guards to put Sibusiso and Jerome in the boot of the car, apparently suspecting them of being criminals. Then his soldiers ordered the driver to move the car down the street to a nearby house and nearby veldt. At this time, a second high ranking officer and neigbour, Brig Gen Nthenjane arrived on the scene - with more armed soldiers, some of them wearing balaclavas. Brig Gen Nthenjane took the men's phones, and called the person they were going to collect the money from and confirmed their story. But despite this, the soldiers then removed the two men from the boot of the car and started assaulting them.They were taken into the veldt and Kgaugelo, the driver, who was left alone as he promised he would not alert SAPS, heard Phetla and Lebaka screaming in the bushes. Kgaugelo told the Generals that his vehicle had a tracking device and that he was just driving the men, and the Generals told him to leave and not tell anyone about what he had seen.



Further information:
Marriam Phetla has agreed to give us an interview, and alsothe sister of Jerome Lebaka
We are asking for permission to film in court on the 19th of September
Gerrie Nel has agreed to give us an interview
We will film recreations of the events on the night in question
We have several important documents to use as evidence, including a piece of the IO's investigation diary where he has been told by the prosecutor to arrest give the generals warning statements and arrest them.

Script:


Murder Cover-Up?
1st Draft Script
26 September 2022
Voice
It’s February. Two friends leave their homes west of Pretoria by car. They drive into an area
owned by the military.
They’re not seen nor heard from again..
Their grieving families have no idea what happened to them. They fear the worst.
This is a story about Sibusiso Phetla and Jerome Lebaka. About an alleged kidnapping, assault
and suspected double murder. About claims that senior military officials are being shielded from
the law.
Link Derek
Nobody knows exactly what happened to Sibusiso and Jerome on that fateful night. All we do know
is that right here, on Magasyn Straat Pretoria, is the last time that they were seen alive. Right
outside the houses of two high ranking army officers. DIP TO BLACK
Voice
Esher Lebaka is Jerome’s sister. Like so many, she’s still searching for answers months after his
disappearance.
Upsound Esther
So we are just this small family of five, nothing interesting about us. He was a quiet guy - shy I
guess, but then this happened.
Voice
Kgaugelo Motsogi is among the few people able to shed light on what happened that night. He’s a
close acquaintance and was driving the car at the time. His version of events on the night of
February 13th alleges shocking abuse of power by military elites.
Upsound Kgaugelo
Derek: What was your mission that night?
Kgaugelo: They approached me, asking me for transport to go to Thaba Tshwane. Jerome said he
was going to pick up money, that’s all we were going to do.
Voice
They were on their way to get cash from Jerome’s uncle. But they apparently took a wrong turn en
route.
Upsound Kgaugelo
At the bottom of the street it’s a cul de sac. So when we got to the cul de sac I realised that we
were lost.
Voice
They ended up in Magasyn street in the Dequar Military Residential area. Kgaugelo says they
pulled over to phone for directions.
Upsound Kgaugelo
Jerome made a phone call to the guy we were going to, and I took the phone, getting directions.
So while I was on the phone, Jerome jumped out of the car, said he was going to take a pee. From
there, I heard a gun shot.
Voice
The man who’d fired the warning shot, whose name is known to Carte Blanche, is a senior army
officer, a Major-General.
Upsound Kgaugelo
Jerome told the guy we are lost, we are looking for directions to go to Thaba Tshwane.
Voice
Soon, more people allegedly arrived on the scene - including armed soldiers. Among them,
another senior officer, a Brigadier General, whose name is also known to us. Sibusiso, Jerome and
Kguagelo were questioned and told to phone Jerome’s uncle to verify their story about being lost.
Upsound Kgaugelo
They called the uncle, and couldn’t understand each other over the phone. So they started beating
up Jerome and Sibusiso.
Voice
Not yet knowing he’d be spared because he was simply the driver, Kgaugelo claims the soldiers
then ordered Jerome and Sibusiso into the boot of the car - in full view of the generals.
Upsound Kgaugelo
Someone said let these two get into the boot. I was shocked, and then I went towards the car I
asked for the key, they said no, we can’t give you the car keys, you will just have to make it turn
then role it down.
Voice
According to Kgaugelo, while the generals went indoors, the car was moved to a cul de sac.
Sound Up Barry Bateman
There are two people who are missing - they’ve been missing since February.
Voice
As baffled by the disappearance as the families are, lobby group Afriforum’s Private Prosecutions
Unit would later take a keen interest in the incident. Barry Bateman is their spokesperson.
Sound Up Barry Bateman
And that’s why we’re representing the families so that they can ultimately get justice, but hopefully
found out where those two missing men are.
Voice
And, no doubt, why things escalated as dramatically as they did. His friends still in the boot,
Kgaugelo claims uniformed men approached from the Brigadier General’s house.
Upsound Kgaugelo
Three guys came running from that same yard towards the car. They were in army clothes but with
their face covered. With black balaclavas or something.
Voice
The masked men allegedly pulled Jerome and Sibusiso from the boot, and led them into nearby
bushes.
Upsound Kgaugelo
Kgaugelo: After 3 minutes or so, for me standing there, they called me into the bush. Telling me
that they are going to let me go. Provided that nobody is going to come looking for these guys. And
if anyone comes looking for these guys, my life will be in danger.
Derek: Do you know if they were still alive when you saw them lying there?
Kgaugelo: Yes they were still alive.
Voice
Shocked and frightened, Kgaugelo fled, believing Jerome and Sibusiso would be arrested and
detained. The following day he called on Esther, and Sibusiso’s mother, Mirriam, to find out if his
friends were ok.
Sound Up Mirriam
Derek: It was on Valentine’s day this year when Esther and Kgaugelo arrived here?
Mirriam: Kgaugelo said I’m not going to tell you the good news. I said hey, what happened if you
say it’s not good news.
Voice
After hearing the story, the women opened a missing person’s case with the police. Kgaugelo
opened a case of assault and kidnapping and three of the foot soldiers who were allegedly
involved have since been arrested.
Link Derek
The three soldiers have been charged with assault GBH and kidnapping here at the Pretoria
Magistrates Court, but questions are being asked as to why the General’s haven’t been arrested.
Voice
That’s why, after several delays, Mirriam approached Afriforum’s Private Prosecutions Unit.
Sound Up Barry
This is a clear case of selective prosecution, where the smaller guy would end up in the courts but
not the big fish, in this case potential generals.
Voice
In a complaint to the SAPS, the unit’s raised concerns about the more junior rank of the
investigating officer.
Sound Up Barry Bateman.
Derek: The prosecutor also raised this as a concern on the 29th of August when you attended
court?
Barry: That’s right, the prosecutor raised the issue of the junior status of the investigating officer as
opposed to the seniority of the general in the SANDF. And that there were concerns that it’s
because of this disparity in the ranks, that the matter wasn’t being adequately investigated.
Voice
Mirriam says it’s something the IO also raised with her.
Sound Up Mirriam
Derek: So he was saying as a sergeant he can’t go and arrest a general?
Mirriam: He can’t go and arrest the general. The senior must go there to arrest the general.
Voice
Is it possible assigning a junior officer was a deliberate attempt at frustrating the case?
Sound Up Barry Bateman
It seems almost inexplicable that you would assign a junior officer to go on investigating a case
where these senior generals are implicated. We strongly believe that this is purposefully done so
as to undermine the ability of the investigator to investigate a very serious crime.
Voice
We asked the police for an interview, but they said they can’t comment on a case not yet finalised
in court.
Link Derek
A lengthy report by Military Police who arrived at the scene that night, raises more suspicions
about the case.
Voice
A parallel investigation by the military reads like a thriller: Military Police who responded to the
disturbance at the generals houses were allegedly prevented from entering the area. The road was
blocked by a vehicle full of armed men identifying themselves as Special Forces operators. The
report also says the vehicle’s number plates were fake.
Small wonder key witness says he’s living in fear.
Sound Up Kgaugelo
Derek: What has life been like since this dreadful incident?
Kgaugelo: I feel threatened because of I’m not just dealing with ordinary people here - it’s the
military men who did this, and who threatened that my life would be in danger if I was to talk about
this.
Voice
Meanwhile grieving families wait for answers no one seems able to give.
Sound Up Mirriam
I’m thinking those things, each and everyday when I sleep. When I cook, I eat, eish, where is,
where is my son?
Voice
Could a gruesome discovery answer that very question? Providing a final, dramatic twist in this
bizarre tale.
Link Derek
On Monday the 19th of September, the state asked for yet another postponement for further
investigation, but a stunning revelation was made, the state prosecutor said that a burnt body had
been found, and sent for DNA testing. A body the state believes, is related to the case.
Sound Up Barry Bateman
We understand according to the submissions made by the prosecutor that there’s something that
has led them to believe that there’s a possible link. We’re now waiting for the DNA results, samples
have been taken from the two parents as well as the body that was discovered.
Voice
The Defence Force hasn’t responded to any of our requests for interviews, neither has the one
general we’ve managed to contact.
But statements made to military police do provide a different version of events.
The Major General says he’d noticed a suspicious plastic bottle outside his gate earlier that
evening. He’d fired the warning shot when he’d noticed the car and its passengers at the exact
spot later on. He also says he’d ordered guards on duty to detain the three men until the military
police arrived.
The guards say all three men were released after the Brigadier General ordered the car to be
moved away from his home later that evening.
None of the soldiers mentioned an assault taking place.
With the next court date scheduled for February next year, it’ll be some time before Esther Lebaka
finds out if the body that’s been discovered is that of her brother.
Sound Up Esther
If it’s really him, then I know, I won’t go or wake up every time thinking that maybe if somebody
knocks on the door it’s him. If I hear a gate open, maybe it’s him. I have closure, I can bury him. If I
miss him I know where to go.
Promo 1 (21 Sec)
Sound Up Gunshot (3 sec)
Voice
A gun shot rings out in the night - setting off a chain of events that leads to the kidnapping, assault
and possibly even murder of two civilians right outside the houses of senior army officers. (12)
Upsound Kgaugelo
And if anyone comes looking for these guys, my life will be in danger. (4)
Voice
We untangle a military mystery.
Promo 2
Voice
Are the Defence Force and Police colluding to prevent an investigation into high level army officers
implicated in a case of kidnapping and assault? (10)
Sound Up Barry Bateman
We strongly believe that this is purposefully done so as to undermine the ability of the investigator
to investigate a very serious crime.
Voice
A closer look at a case of alleged selective prosecution.
Promo 3
The disappearance of two men in Pretoria has led to allegations of the assault and kidnapping of
civilians by members of the South African National Defence Force.

We’re now waiting for the DNA results, samples have been taken from the two parents as well as the body that was discovered. Voice The Defence Force hasn’t responded to any of our requests for interviews, neither has the one general we’ve managed to contact. But statements made to military police do provide a different version of events. The Major General says he’d noticed a suspicious plastic bottle outside his gate earlier that evening. He’d fired the warning shot when he’d noticed the car and its passengers at the exact spot later on. He also says he’d ordered guards on duty to detain the three men until the military police arrived. The guards say all three men were released after the Brigadier General ordered the car to be moved away from his home later that evening. None of the soldiers mentioned an assault taking place. With the next court date scheduled for February next year, it’ll be some time before Esther Lebaka finds out if the body that’s been discovered is that of her brother. I have closure, I can bury him. If I miss him I know where to go. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Private prosecutor Gerrie Nel has accussed the SAPS and SANDF of colluding to protect two high ranking SANDF members from criminal prosecution in a kidnapping and assault and possibly murder case.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: After the alleged kidnapping and assault of two men, Sibusiso Phetla and Jerome Lebaka, in February this year, the victims have never been heard of again and suspicions are that they were murdered. It has since come to light that Phetla and Lebaka were mistaken for burglars outside a SANDF general's home, where they were allegedly assaulted by soldiers protecting the general. Another general has also been implicated. While the soldiers who were under the command of the generals have been arrested and are facing charges of assault and kidnapping, the general's have not - raising concerns that the generals are being protected.
metadata.Summary: According to a witness,(a man who drove them) Phetla and Lebaka got lost on their way to Thaba Tshwane in Pretoria in February. They ended up in Magasyn Street, in the Dequar Military Residential area. Kgaugelo, the driver, stopped the car next to a house. Unbeknownst to him, it was the home of Major General Hlongwa, a high ranking official in the SANDF. Apparently they stopped to phone for directions to their destination. As the men were making the phone call, they heard a gunshot from Maj Gen Hlongwa's house - apparently the General had fired the shot to scare them off. Almost immediately their car was surrounded by armed military personnel, guards on duty at the General's house. General Hlongwa ordered his guards to put Sibusiso and Jerome in the boot of the car, apparently suspecting them of being criminals. Then his soldiers ordered the driver to move the car down the street to a nearby house and nearby veldt. At this time, a second high ranking officer and neigbour, Brig Gen Nthenjane arrived on the scene - with more armed soldiers, some of them wearing balaclavas. Brig Gen Nthenjane took the men's phones, and called the person they were going to collect the money from and confirmed their story. But despite this, the soldiers then removed the two men from the boot of the car and started assaulting them.They were taken into the veldt and Kgaugelo, the driver, who was left alone as he promised he would not alert SAPS, heard Phetla and Lebaka screaming in the bushes. Kgaugelo told the Generals that his vehicle had a tracking device and that he was just driving the men, and the Generals told him to leave and not tell anyone about what he had seen.
